description:
Count how many jobs match a search without returning full results. Returns structured JSON.

Use this when the user asks "how many jobs..." (in any language), including
salary-constrained counts like "how many jobs pay at least 60k?" or
"how many jobs advertise a salary at all?" (use has_salary=True).

Args:
    q: Search keywords, e.g. "Softwareentwickler Python"
    location: City or region, e.g. "München", "Bodensee"
    working_plan: "Vollzeit", "Teilzeit", "Homeoffice", or "Minijob"
    job_offer_type: "Arbeitsplatz", "Ausbildung", "Praktikum", "Freiberuflich", "Werkstudent", "Trainee", "Duales-Studium"
    min_salary: Minimum ANNUAL gross salary in EUR (optional), e.g. 60000.
                Filtered server-side with the same semantics as search_jobs:
                monthly/hourly amounts are normalised to a yearly figure first,
                and salary ranges match on overlap. A job with range
                30.000–45.000 € is counted at min_salary=40000 (ranges overlap).
    max_salary: Maximum annual gross salary in EUR (optional, same semantics).
                A job with range 30.000–45.000 € is NOT counted at max_salary=25000.
    has_salary: If True, count only jobs that advertise a salary at all
                (regardless of amount). If False, count only jobs WITHOUT a
                salary. Leave unset to ignore. Use this for "how many jobs
                have a salary?"; combine with min_salary/max_salary as needed.

Returns:
    On success: {"count": int, "filters": {"q": str|null, "location": str|null,
                                           "working_plan": str|null, "job_offer_type": str|null,
                                           "min_salary": float|null, "max_salary": float|null,
                                           "has_salary": bool|null}}
    On error:   {"error": str}
name: count_jobs
title: Count jobs
